tools.name: business_days
tools.description: Count business days between two dates, or find the date a number of business days before or after a date, skipping Saturdays, Sundays and US federal holidays on the days they are observed. Send start and either end (to count) or add_business_days (to step; negative steps back). Holidays follow 5 U.S.C. 6103 as federal offices observe them (Saturday holiday on the Friday before, Sunday holiday on the Monday after) or, if you choose, as the Federal Reserve Banks do (a Saturday holiday is not moved). Get back the count both ways (both dates included, and start left out), or the result date, with the weekend days and every holiday skipped by name and date. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/business-days). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

end.description: To count: the end date, YYYY-MM-DD, on or after start. Send end or add_business_days, not both.

add_business_days.description: To step: how many business days after start (negative: before start), not counting start itself. 1 = the next business day. Not 0.

holidays.description: federal_offices (default): 5 U.S.C. 6103 holidays, Saturday ones on the Friday before and Sunday ones on the Monday after. federal_reserve_banks: the same holidays, Sunday ones on Monday, Saturday ones not moved.

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'notice period' (your own text, echoed).

tools.name: frcp_deadline
tools.description: Count a federal civil deadline the way Fed. R. Civ. P. 6 counts it. Send the trigger date (the event: service, entry of judgment, a hearing date), the number of days, and whether the period runs after or before the event. The trigger day is left out, every day is counted, and a last day on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the next day that is not one (backward for periods before an event). Federal legal holidays are built in on the days they are observed; send state holidays, days declared holidays by the President or Congress, and days the clerk's office was inaccessible as lists. If the time runs after being served by mail, by leaving it with the clerk, or by other means consented to, 3 days are added under Rule 6(d). Get back the deadline, every day skipped and why, when the last day ends, and, for a period after an event, an earlier date to file by when the deadline moved past a holiday observed on another day than its date. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/frcp-deadline). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

trigger_date.description: Date of the event that starts the count (service, entry of the order, the hearing), YYYY-MM-DD. From 2016-12-01.

days.description: The period in days, as the rule, order or statute states it (14, 21, 28, 30, 90 ...).

direction.description: after (default): act within N days after the event. before: act at least N days before the event (the trigger_date is then the event, such as a hearing).

served_by.description: Only when the time runs after being served: how the paper was served under Rule 5(b)(2). mail, left_with_clerk and other_consented add 3 days (Rule 6(d)); electronic and in_person (handed over or left at the office or home) add none.

state_holidays.description: Holidays declared by the state where the district court sits, YYYY-MM-DD (up to 40). Counted only for periods after an event (Rule 6(a)(6)(C)).

declared_holidays.description: Other days declared a holiday by the President or Congress (an Executive order closing federal offices, a national day of mourning), YYYY-MM-DD (up to 40). Counted both ways (Rule 6(a)(6)(B)).

clerk_inaccessible.description: Days the clerk's office was inaccessible (weather, a filing-system outage), YYYY-MM-DD (up to 40). A filing deadline on such a day moves to the next accessible day (Rule 6(a)(3)). Periods after an event only.

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'answer to complaint' (your own text, echoed; not a party name).

tools.name: trust_three_way_reconciliation
tools.description: Reconcile a lawyer's client trust (IOLTA) account three ways as of a date: the adjusted bank balance, the trust account's general ledger (journal) balance, and the total of the client ledgers. Get back the three balances, whether they are identical, each difference, every client ledger below zero (one client's money covering another's), outstanding items older than the age you set, and hints for finding a difference (a single item, an item entered with the wrong sign, a transposed figure). Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/trust-three-way-reconciliation). ref.description: Check number or deposit reference with at least one digit (up to 8 digits in a row, letters only as abbreviations up to 4), not a payee or client name.

date.description: Optional date written or deposited, YYYY-MM-DD (on or before as_of).

other_deductions.description: Other deductions to subtract from the statement balance (up to 200), as your reconciliation lists them.

tools.name: contract_notice_dates
tools.description: Work out a contract's term end dates, renewal dates and the last day to give notice of non-renewal. Send the start date, the initial term in months, whether it renews automatically, the renewal term, and the notice days (notice at least N days before the term ends, or before the renewal date). Optionally send as_of to see the current term, whether the notice window is still open and the next notice deadline, max_renewals if the contract caps them, and ny_gol_5_903 to get the window in which a provider of a New York service, maintenance or repair contract must send its reminder. Weekend notice deadlines are flagged with the Friday before as a safe send-by date. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/contract-notice-dates). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

start_date.description: First day of the contract's initial term, YYYY-MM-DD.

initial_term_months.description: Initial term in months (12 for one year, 36 for three years).

auto_renews.description: true if the contract renews automatically unless notice is given; false if it simply ends.

renewal_term_months.description: Each renewal term in months (default: the same as the initial term).

notice_days.description: Days of notice needed to stop the renewal (for auto-renewing contracts). 'At least 60 days before' = 60.

notice_counted_from.description: term_end (default): N days before the last day of the term. renewal_date: N days before the first day of the next term (one day later). Use the words of the contract.

max_renewals.description: Optional: the most renewal terms the contract allows (0 = none). Leave out if renewals are unlimited.

as_of.description: Optional date to check against (today, say), YYYY-MM-DD.

renewals_to_show.description: How many renewal terms to list after the first one shown (default 3, up to 40).

ny_gol_5_903.description: true to add the New York General Obligations Law 5-903 reminder window (service, maintenance or repair contracts for property; renewal terms over one month).

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'copier lease' (your own text, echoed; not a party name).

tools.name: federal_prompt_pay_deadline
tools.description: Work out when a US federal agency must pay a contractor under the Prompt Payment Act, and the late-payment interest if it paid late. Payment types: supplies_services_invoice (30 days after a proper invoice, with the 7-day constructive-acceptance rule), construction_progress (14 days after a proper progress payment request), construction_retainage (30 days after the contracting officer approves release), construction_final (the later of 30 days after the proper invoice and 30 days after acceptance, acceptance deemed on the 7th day after completion), and subcontractor (the prime pays its subcontractor within 7 days of being paid). Send the dates you have; get back the due date, the date payment may still be made without interest when the due date is a weekend or federal holiday, and, with paid_date, amount and the Treasury Prompt Payment rate you send, the days late and the interest (30-day compounding, 360-day year, at most one year). The live Treasury rate is not fetched: send the rate in effect on the day after the due date. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/federal-prompt-pay-deadline). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

payment_type.description: supplies_services_invoice, construction_progress, construction_retainage, construction_final or subcontractor.

invoice_received.description: Date the designated billing office received the proper invoice or progress payment request, YYYY-MM-DD. If the office did not stamp a receipt date, send the date on the invoice (5 CFR 1315.4(b)(2)).

delivered_or_completed.description: Date the goods were delivered or the work or services were completed, YYYY-MM-DD (supplies_services_invoice, construction_final).

accepted.description: Date the agency actually accepted the goods or work, YYYY-MM-DD (supplies_services_invoice, construction_final).

acceptance_period_days.description: Only if the contract sets an acceptance period longer than 7 days: its length in days (supplies_services_invoice).

release_approved.description: Date the contracting officer approved release of retained amounts, YYYY-MM-DD (construction_retainage).

prime_paid.description: Date the prime contractor received the agency's payment that covers the subcontractor's work, YYYY-MM-DD (subcontractor).

contract_due_date.description: Only if the contract itself names the payment due date, YYYY-MM-DD; used as given, but never before the period starts, and for construction_progress only later than the 14th day (supplies_services_invoice, construction_progress, construction_retainage).

paid_date.description: Optional: date paid (check date, or EFT settlement date), YYYY-MM-DD. A date before the payment period starts is read as an early payment and said so.

amount.description: Optional, with paid_date: the amount paid late (the principal interest runs on).

annual_rate_percent.description: Optional, with paid_date and amount: the Treasury Prompt Payment interest rate in percent a year in effect on the day after the due date (4.75 for 4.75%). Not fetched; Treasury publishes it twice a year.

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'pay app 7' (your own text, echoed; no contract or invoice numbers longer than 6 digits).

tools.name: business_days_calculator
tools.description: Count the business days between two dates, or find the date a number of business days after or before a date, for a country and (United Kingdom) a nation. Send start, country, and either end (to count) or add_business_days (to step; negative steps back); region ENG, WLS, SCT or NIR for the United Kingdom. Optional extra_days_off: your own closing days. Covered: US (United States (federal)), GB (United Kingdom), DE (Germany (national days)), FR (France), IE (Ireland). Any other country is refused, not guessed. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/business-days-calculator). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166 country code: US, GB (or UK), DE, FR, IE.

region.description: United Kingdom only, required: ENG, WLS, SCT or NIR. Not used for the other countries.

end.description: To count: the end date, YYYY-MM-DD, on or after start. Send end or add_business_days, not both.

add_business_days.description: To step: how many business days after start (negative: before start), not counting start itself. 1 = the next business day. Not 0.

extra_days_off.description: Optional: your own non-working days (company closings, a local holiday), each YYYY-MM-DD; skipped like holidays.

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'notice period' (your own text, echoed).

tools.name: statute_limitations_date
tools.description: Find the last day to file when a limitation period runs from an accrual date. Send the accrual date and the period you have already looked up, as years, months and/or days (for example 2 years, or 30 days). The accrual day is not counted. If the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or a holiday you list, it moves to the next day that is none of those (switch this off if your rule does not move it). Get back the last day to file with its weekday, the day before the move and why it moved, and, if you send today's date, how many days are left. When the last day does not exist in its month (29 Feb + 1 year, 31 Jan + 1 month) the answer says so and shows the other common reading. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/statute-limitations-date). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

accrual_date.description: The date the period starts from (the claim accrued, the injury, the breach, the event), YYYY-MM-DD. The tool does not decide when a claim accrues.

years.description: Years in the period (0 if none).

months.description: Months in the period (0 if none).

days.description: Days in the period, counted after the years and months (0 if none).

weekend_rollover.description: true (default): a last day on a Saturday, Sunday or listed holiday moves forward to the next day that is none of those. false: the date is not moved.

holidays.description: Optional: court holidays that matter here, each YYYY-MM-DD (up to 40). The tool knows no holiday: you send them. Used only when weekend_rollover is on.

as_of.description: Optional: today's date (or the date you want to measure from), YYYY-MM-DD, to get the days left.

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'contract claim' (your own text, echoed back; not a party name).

tools.name: citation_format_check

tools.name: docket_days_rule
tools.description: Count a deadline that runs a number of days after service, using the numbers your court rule or statute states (state court, agency, arbitration, or a court order). Send the service date, the period in days (calendar or court days), the days your rule adds for the service method (mail, electronic, overnight), whether those days are added after the period's last day has been moved off a weekend or holiday (the federal Rule 6(d) way) or counted on together with the period before any move, and the holidays your court closes on. U.S. federal holidays (on their observed days) are built in and can be turned off. Get back the deadline, its weekday, every day skipped and why, and each step of the count. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/docket-days-rule). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

service_date.description: Date of service (the day that starts the count; it is not counted), YYYY-MM-DD.

days.description: The period your rule states, in days (10, 14, 20, 21, 30 ...).

count_in.description: calendar_days (default): every day counts. court_days: only days that are not a Saturday, Sunday or holiday count.

added_days.description: Days your rule adds for how the paper was served (for example 3 under the federal rule for mail; your state's number for mail or electronic service). 0 if none.

added_count_in.description: Whether the added days are calendar_days (default) or court_days, as your rule says.

added_days_when.description: after_rollover (default; Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(d)): find the period's deadline first, moving it off a weekend or holiday, then add the days. with_period: add the days straight on from the period's last day, then move the result once.

rollover.description: forward (default): a last day on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday moves to the next day that is not one. none: no move (only if your rule says so).

us_federal_holidays.description: Count the 11 U.S. federal holidays, on the days federal offices observe them, as holidays (default true). Set false for a court that does not close on them, and send its holidays instead.

holidays.description: Other days your court is closed or your rule calls holidays (state holidays, the day after Thanksgiving, closures), YYYY-MM-DD (up to 60).

rule_cited.description: Optional: the rule you are applying, e.g. 'Tex. R. Civ. P. 21a' (your own text, echoed; it is not read or checked).

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'response to motion' (your own text, echoed; not a party name).

tools.name: lien_deadline_dates
tools.description: Count mechanics lien (construction lien) notice and filing deadlines from the dates of a job. Send the last day you furnished labor or materials (and, if a step needs them, the first day, the date an owner's notice of completion or termination was recorded, or the date your lien was recorded), plus each step with the count YOUR state's statute gives: a number of days, a number of months, or a day of a later month (the Texas form '15th day of the 3rd month after the month the work was done'). Get back each deadline, its weekday, whether it falls on a weekend or US federal holiday, the next business day if you say your state extends such deadlines, and, with as_of, the days left or the days past. The tool does not know any state's counts: you send them. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/lien-deadline-dates). Not legal, tax or financial advice.

first_work_date.description: First day labor, services or materials were furnished (for preliminary-notice steps counted from the start), YYYY-MM-DD.

completion_notice_date.description: Date the owner's notice of completion, cessation or termination was recorded, if a step counts from it, YYYY-MM-DD.

count.description: The number from the statute: days (1 to 3650) or months (1 to 120).

unit.description: days (N days after), months (same day N months after; last day of the month when that day does not exist), month_day (day_of_month of the Nth month after the month of the start date).

from.description: Which date the count starts from: last_work (default), first_work, completion_notice or lien_recorded.

day_of_month.description: Only for unit month_day: the day of that month (15 for 'the 15th day'); last day of the month when the month is shorter.

weekend_holiday_rule.description: none (default): the deadline stays on the counted day, even a weekend or holiday. next_business_day: only if YOUR state's time-computation statute extends a deadline that falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday.

extra_holidays.description: Optional: your state's legal holidays that are not US federal holidays (up to 40 dates). They count as non-business days.

items.description: A state or local legal holiday, YYYY-MM-DD.

as_of.description: Optional: today's date (or any date), YYYY-MM-DD, to get days left or days past for each step.

tools.name: cobra_notice_dates
tools.description: Count the federal COBRA deadlines after a qualifying event under an employer group health plan. as_of.description: Optional: today's date (or any date), YYYY-MM-DD, to get the days left until each date or the days past it.

tools.name: fcra_dispute_dates
tools.description: Count the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act dates for a consumer's dispute of an item on a credit report. Send the date the credit reporting agency received the dispute and, if you have them, the date the reinvestigation was completed and today's date. Get back the day the reinvestigation must be complete (30 days), the latest day if the consumer sent more information during the 30 days (45 days), the day the results must reach the consumer (5 business days after completion, skipping weekends and federal holidays), each date's weekday, weekend and holiday marks, whether the reinvestigation finished in time, and with as_of the days left or past. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/fcra-dispute-dates). Not legal, tax or financial advice.

dispute_received.description: Date the consumer reporting agency received the consumer's dispute, YYYY-MM-DD.

reinvestigation_completed.description: Optional: date the reinvestigation was completed, YYYY-MM-DD. Gives the results-sent date and whether the 30 and 45 day dates were met.

as_of.description: Optional: today's date (or any date), YYYY-MM-DD, to get the days left until each date or the days past it.

tools.name: settlement_split
tools.description: Do the arithmetic of a contingent-fee settlement closing statement. Send the gross settlement, the attorney fee percent, the case costs and the liens or other deductions (all amounts, no names). Get back the attorney fee, the net to the client, each line and the total deducted, the client's share of the gross in percent, and a flag when the deductions are more than the settlement. It is arithmetic only, not legal advice: the signed fee agreement controls how the fee is figured. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/settlement-split). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

fee_percent.description: Attorney fee percent from the fee agreement, 0 to 100 (up to 4 decimals).

liens.description: Liens, medical reimbursements and other deductions paid out of the settlement (default 0).

label.description: Optional label (your own text, up to 6 digits in a row; echoed).
